question.text: A PM uses a PROTECTIVE PUT on a bond futures position to hedge large adverse rate moves. The MAXIMUM loss is limited to:

answer.text: The premium paid for the put

explanation.text: The Logic: A protective put combines a long position in the underlying with a long put option, which provides downside protection at the cost of the premium paid. The workbook's protective-put example shows that the downside loss is limited to the premium paid. The Trap: "Unlimited" applies to naked short positions, not to a long position hedged with a put; "zero" ignores the premium cost that defines the maximum loss. Note: Page 322 illustrates protective-put mechanics with the premium as the loss floor; page 350 applies protective puts to portfolio protection.
